videos.title: My Stock just BLUE UP‼️
AMD Just FLIPPED THE ENTIRE MARKET & ITS OWN STOCK‼️

key_points: AMD delivered strong quarterly earnings with 45% YoY revenue growth and guided Q4 revenue to ~$17B (~66% YoY growth).
Data Center segment revenue surged 97% YoY to $8.5B, driven by strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct MI450/MI350 GPUs.
Jeremy holds over $1.2M of AMD in his public account (and significantly more privately), maintaining a long-term target of $1,000+ per share.
Laggard segments like client and gaming are expected to inflect positively with easy comparisons by 2027.
Jeremy dismisses political and election worries as temporary noise that will not derail long-term hyperscaler capex spending.
Reiterating Bill Ackman's commentary on retail dominance, Jeremy notes Amazon remains one of his biggest positions due to its irreplaceable supply chain and AWS.
analysis.market_view: Jeremy remains bullish on big tech and semiconductors, arguing that market volatility around elections or politics is transient noise and that hyperscaler AI capex will continue to expand aggressively over the next several years.

stock_moves.position_note: Holds $1.24M+ in public portfolio (average cost $101.41) plus more in private portfolios
stock_moves.rationale: AMD reported exceptional earnings with 97% YoY data center revenue growth, strong operating leverage, and guidance well above consensus, solidifying a path toward a $1,000+ long-term stock price.

stock_moves.position_note: One of his biggest positions across public and private portfolios
stock_moves.rationale: Amazon possesses an unreplicable supply chain and logistics distribution network that cements retail dominance alongside the profitability of AWS.
Mentioned as an inferior competitor that has consistently lost market share to AMD for nearly a decade.
Referenced as the premier leader in AI training hardware that is also poised to report blowout earnings.

analysis.summary: Jeremy breaks down AMD's latest earnings report, highlighting massive acceleration in its data center revenue and strong forward guidance that outpaces Wall Street expectations. He reviews the income statement, explains why AMD should not be conflated with Intel, and notes that AMD is well positioned for the upcoming AI inference and robotics waves. Jeremy also reacts to CNBC clips featuring analyst Stacy Rasgon, Fundstrat's Tom Lee, and Pershing Square's Bill Ackman discussing AI capex spending and election impacts. Throughout the video, Jeremy emphasizes looking past short-term macro noise and affirms his long-term conviction in AMD and Amazon.

videos.title: If you own stocks DO THIS BEFORE ITS TOO LATE‼️

key_points: Market decline in the QQQ is a tech sector rotation rather than a full market crash, as consumer and housing stocks are holding up strong.
Semiconductor comeback is anticipated to begin shortly, running into early 2027.
Maintains long-term conviction in AMD despite short-term volatility, seeing $1,000+ per share in the coming years.
Palantir's revenue growth is expected to decelerate from recent 90%+ peaks, making it a HOLD between $125 and $200 (buy under $125, sell over $200).
Views Celsius Holdings as analogous to Palantir in 2022, seeing potential to reach $100+ over the long term.
Highlights Estée Lauder as a high-margin turnaround play with strong earnings growth and significant upside from current levels.
analysis.market_view: The QQQ is in an official small correction down 10% from highs, but the overall market is not in a systemic crash like 2008 or 2020 because capital is simply rotating out of AI/tech and into defensive, consumer, and housing names.

stock_moves.position_note: Portfolio position shown worth ~$1.19M; plans to hold long-term to $1,000+
stock_moves.rationale: Believes Wall Street will inevitably return to AMD as semiconductors enter a multi-month boom cycle, maintaining a multi-year target of $1,000+ per share.

stock_moves.position_note: Position worth ~$182k; would buy under $125 and sell over $200 over the next 12 months
stock_moves.rationale: While current numbers are strong, revenue growth is likely facing deceleration from 90%+ down into the double digits alongside high valuation and expanding cost of revenue.

stock_moves.position_note: Public account position at ~$254k; currently in 'acquisition mode'
stock_moves.rationale: Sees Celsius trading cheaply in the $20s similar to Palantir in 2022 when sentiment was bottomed out, believing long-term growth and margin expansion will drive shares to $100+.
Delivered A-grade earnings with gross margin expanding to 75.7% and net earnings surging 5x year-over-year, offering potential to double or triple over time.
Now trades as an AI play due to massive energy and data-center power generation equipment demand rather than a traditional economic bellwether.

analysis.summary: Jeremy addresses the recent market downturn and correction in major tech and semiconductor stocks, clarifying that the market is experiencing sector rotation rather than an outright broad crash. He explains that non-tech sectors like housing, retail, and beverages are performing well despite the tech selloff. Jeremy reaffirms his long-term bullish stance on AMD, outlines his exact price targets for Palantir (buy under $125, sell over $200), names Celsius as his 'next Palantir,' and highlights Estée Lauder as an undervalued hidden gem following strong earnings.

videos.title: Tech Stocks Plunge, Here’s What’s Next
I Sold it all

key_points: Sold entire position in ServiceNow (NOW) for roughly $75,300 to take profits amid slowing growth and question marks around enterprise execution.
Reallocated proceeds by buying $20,000 of Celsius (CELH), $27,600 of American Express (AXP), and $27,800 of Netflix (NFLX).
Views Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOG) as long-term steals despite near-term market panic over ballooning AI capital expenditures.
Argues that Intel's (INTC) poor results won't hurt AMD (AMD) long term because AMD continues to capture market share in CPUs and GPUs.
Identifies broader weakness in consumer product spending across retail and tech as a sign of an economic slowdown rather than company-specific failures.
analysis.market_view: Sees current macroeconomic weakness reflected in softening consumer product sales across multiple retail and tech companies, alongside market anxiety regarding aggressive AI capital expenditure plans reducing hyperscaler free cash flows.

stock_moves.rationale: Took profits after a large post-earnings drop, citing deceleration in growth, preference for Salesforce, and more attractive risk/reward elsewhere.
Used proceeds from the ServiceNow sale to add to a high-conviction growth holding expected to generate strong multi-year returns.
Reinvested capital into a premier, top-tier business with durable fundamentals.

stock_moves.position_note: Bought 45 shares ($27,847.80); position now just under $180k
stock_moves.rationale: Added to a core winner using proceeds from the ServiceNow liquidation.
Considers the post-earnings pullback a long-term buying opportunity despite weak product sales and massive upcoming AI capex spend.

stock_moves.position_note: $62k position remaining after earlier profit taking
stock_moves.rationale: Acknowledges capex fears will hit free cash flow in the medium term, but considers the core search and cloud business an attractive multi-year hold.
Believes Intel's weakness is AMD's long-term strength as AMD consistently takes market share across CPUs and data center GPUs.
Trusts Marc Benioff and Salesforce's business model more than ServiceNow in the enterprise software space.
Ran projections concluding Microsoft is an okay buy capable of delivering mid-teens compound annual growth, though less attractive than Amazon.
Criticized Intel as a declining business that relied on government intervention and continues to face structural headwinds.

analysis.summary: Jeremy discusses recent tech market volatility following earnings reports from Google, ServiceNow, Intel, and Amazon. He analyzes big tech earnings, arguing that consumer product softness signals a weakening general economy while massive rising AI capex spending is alarming Wall Street over free cash flow. Consequently, Jeremy decided to completely sell out of his ServiceNow (NOW) position to take profits and reallocated the capital into heavy additions of Celsius (CELH), American Express (AXP), and Netflix (NFLX).
